summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with acute chest pain and shortness of breath during a dialysis session. Evaluation revealed mild troponin elevation without EKG changes, hypertension, and signs of fluid overload including pulmonary edema on imaging. Symptoms were attributed to demand ischemia secondary to hypervolemia. Ultrafiltration removed 4.1 liters of fluid, leading to resolution of symptoms and improvement in vital signs and labs. She remained stable throughout the hospital stay with controlled blood pressure, improved respiratory status, and no further cardiac events. She was discharged to an extended care facility with instructions for strict fluid and salt restriction, daily weight monitoring, and continuation of home medications with adjustments to sevelamer and insulin dosing.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Diabetes with renal manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Coronary atherosclerosis of unspecified type of vessel, native or graft
Late effects of cerebrovascular disease, hemiplegia affecting unspecified side
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
